<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 39 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dd72a047f83cf8e6b9826183bd4de304d4f16957` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0135bbfecaa297ad0deec697beef73beca176857` — the merge of head `4fc739dfbf28939a54b641025938f075e28d5534` into base `dd72a047f83cf8e6b9826183bd4de304d4f16957`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0135bbfecaa297ad0deec697beef73beca176857 && git checkout 0135bbfecaa297ad0deec697beef73beca176857
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dd72a047f83cf8e6b9826183bd4de304d4f16957 4fc739dfbf28939a54b641025938f075e28d5534 && git checkout -B drift-repro dd72a047f83cf8e6b9826183bd4de304d4f16957 && git merge --no-ff 4fc739dfbf28939a54b641025938f075e28d5534

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dd72a047f83cf8e6b9826183bd4de304d4f16957
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dd72a047f83cf8e6b9826183bd4de304d4f16957` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

ACCEPT · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `marchtian` · `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH` · 2026-10-18T15:28Z · head `4fc739dfbf`. The seat's own review at `TIER_DEFAULT`: `--tier` read no path-derived mandate over the 9 paths, and no published schema or governed text is touched (the eight codes are already on `main`, `0b44840df`). It lands through the merge queue once every check on this head is green.

- **Shape:** a draft PR to `main`. Its first line is `Fixes #24243`, and that is the only closing keyword in the body. `Clause-②: no` is at a line start in the body and in the changeset (`@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch). Card and PR assignee: `marchtian`. Not governed: `check-governed-merges` reads 0 of 9 paths, and 686 changed lines ≤ 3000.
- **The spec seat's table (`6248819342`), each stamp read by the seat in `auth-manager.ts`:**
  - `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` on both phone-OTP walls, through ONE constant, `PHONE_OTP_SEND_REFUSAL_CODE`, so #2814's two walls stay indistinguishable.
  - `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` on the slug guard's read fault.
  - `VALIDATION_ERROR` on the reserved `__global__` identifier.
  - `ORGANIZATION_CREATION_DISABLED`, `INVITE_PLACEMENT_UNSUPPORTED`, `INVITE_PLACEMENT_OUTSIDE_ISSUER_SCOPE` and `ORGANIZATION_SLUG_LOCKED_BY_ACTIVE_ENVIRONMENTS` on their throws.

  Each is a module constant: the four registered codes are typed `RegisteredErrorCode` and the four standard ones `StandardErrorCode`. A removed ledger row fails `tsc`. Every status is unchanged.
- **The three implementer notes, met:**
  1. **The placement catch splits on the gate's own verdict.** `isInvitationPlacementGateRefusal` reads `code === 'PERMISSION_DENIED'` structurally. The seat checked both sides on `main`: plugin-security's `PermissionDeniedError` declares `code = 'PERMISSION_DENIED'` (`errors.ts:42`), and the store fault `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` declares `code = 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'` (`core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.ts:96`, `:149`). So a store fault cannot pass as a refusal. It now answers 503 with its code and `cause`, and its message is not relayed. This is the PR's one behaviour change, and it narrows a false refusal.
  2. **The `:3668` message** no longer says environments "still reference" the organization or prescribes renaming hostnames, and the slug guard's read-fault message lost the same wording. The comment above `SMS_QUOTA_EXCEEDED_CODE` no longer calls it an ADR-0112 code.
  3. **The console's map row** is objectui's, and the seat files it at landing. It is not in this PR.
- **Pins:**
  - `api-error-code.pin.test.ts`, a test and not a gate, walks every `new APIError(` in `plugin-auth/src` and requires a `code`, reading the two `judgeHeldSession` relays as coded.
  - Its control: with `auth-manager.ts` swapped to the base blob, the pin lists exactly the eight positions of `6245494426`.
  - Wire pins on a stock showcase boot reach the reserved identifier, creation disabled and the placement scope refusal. The OTP walls, the slug guard's two throws and placement-unsupported are unit-pinned, each with a reason.
  - Two ablations, each restored blob-equal to HEAD: dropping the `:3668` stamp turns the pin red at that one site, and dropping the catch's guard turns the store-fault pin from 503 to 403.
- **Gates on this head:** 36 checks succeeded and 5 were skipped by design (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance: the roster set; Build Docs ran, since the docs page is in the diff, and passed). There were no failures, and the required contexts are green. Locally the dev derived 99 families on this head, ran all 99, and all exited 0 (`--ran`: 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN). Two first exited 3 on an unbuilt prerequisite and passed after it was built.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - **`StandardErrorCode` typing for the four standard codes:** they are not ledger members. #23945 typed its `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` the same way.
  - **`content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`, outside the claim's surface:** this PR made two of its sentences false. The SMS quota "answers `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`", and `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` "is never flat". The edit only restates what the wire now carries, and it is not governed.
  - **The changeset leaves out the SMS invitation:** `admin-import-users` catches that send's failure into a per-row `INVITE_SMS_FAILED`, so the 429 never reaches its wire.
  - **`origin/main` (`51ad8e4fb`) was merged before the PR opened,** carrying PR #24325's four `plugin-auth` files with no overlap, and everything was re-run on `4fc739dfb`. The PR body's phrase "the head this PR opens with" is one push behind that. The seat leaves the body as is, since the head is named here.
- **Out-of-scope findings, with their carriers:** the console's `ORGANIZATION_CREATION_DISABLED` → `workspace.multiOrgDisabled` map row (the spec seat's note 3). The seat files it in objectstack-ai/objectui at landing.
